author: Daniel Hager
title: Brent Venables considered benching John Mateer at halftime of Georgia game, decided against it - NewsBreak
text:
By Daniel Hager ,
9 hours ago
Sep 26, 2026; Athens, Georgia, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) warms up before a game against the Georgia Bulldogs at Sanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Saturday’s game between Oklahoma and No. 2 Georgia served as one of the worst in the career of Sooner quarterback John Mateer . Mateer completed 25/34 passes for 231 yards and two touchdowns, but also tossed an interception and lost two fumbles. One of those fumbles resulted in a touchdown return for the Georgia defense, which helped contribute to the 41-13 Bulldog victory.
The 28-point defeat for the Sooners marked their biggest since their 31-point loss to No. 1 Texas on Oct. 12, 2024. Following the game, OU head coach Brent Venables revealed that he nearly benched Mateer at halftime , but ultimately decided against it. When discussing Mateer’s confidence at the moment, he declared that “It’s certainly not sky high.”

Mateer entered his second season as Oklahoma ‘s starting quarterback fresh off a run to the College Football Playoff in 2025. With all eyes on back-to-back appearances, the Little Elm, Tx. native just hasn’t played up to expectations set for him. Across four games, Mateer is completing just 62.7% of his passes, and he has yet to hit the 250-plus yard passing mark.
Oklahoma opened its season ranked No. 9 in the country, but four weeks into the season, the program finds itself unranked and floundering. The Sooners sit at 2-2 on the year, with games against No. 1 Texas , a likely-ranked Kentucky team, No. 24 Mississippi State , and No. 21 Florida . If things continue to go the way of going off the rails for the Sooners, the 2026 season could mark Brent Venables ‘ third six-or-less win season across his five-year stint at Oklahoma .
Brent Venables just inked extension with Oklahoma prior to season Brent Venables ‘ new six-year, $63 million contract was officially approved by the OU Board of Regents in mid-Sept., setting him up to be the Sooners’ head coach for the long-haul. A 28-point loss to Georgia coming off a 14-6 win over New Mexico and a 17-10 loss to Michigan certainly isn’t what Oklahoma fans were expecting following the extension.
“We’re in this moment of incredible turbulence. It’s going to find a level somewhere, and there’s nobody I’d rather have at the helm of that leading our team than Brent Venables , right now — his steady hand, his unbelievable energy, best defensive mind in the country, a head coach that is growing in remarkable ways,” OU President Joe Harroz said.
“I think we’ve all seen his growth… we’re at a moment where I’m really proud and confident, and I think it’s a moment where stability and strength and all of that matters more than it ever will… He’s our head coach.”
Oklahoma will look to bounce back from the blowout loss next Saturday against No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. The Longhorns are 4-0, and boast two victories over top-15 opponents this season (No. 1 Ohio State and No. 14 Tennessee ).
